summary: Sharp spike of 5xx on embedding-stream upload during tenant warmup — apigw WINDOW_UPDATE burst -> fd exhaustion -> runtime restarts
summary_brief: Customer reports elevated 5xx on embedding-stream route during nightly warmup; load correlates with WINDOW_UPDATE bursts from mobile SDK clients leading to accept-queue growth and runtime fd exhaustion.
description:
Issue summary:
AcmeMaps (dedicated) experienced a rapid increase in 5xx responses on the /v1/embeddings:stream-upload route during their nightly warmup window (02:10–02:40 UTC). Error rate rose from ~0.2% to ~14% for a 20-minute window.

Impact:
- Customer-facing failures on embedding uploads and intermittent streaming disconnects for map annotation features.
- Elevated retries causing downstream latency and billing noise.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in eu-west (customer_dedicated_pool-12).
- Affected model: openembed-1-large (quantized).
- Recent config rollout: apigw keepalive-reaper v2.3.1 deployed at 2026-03-12T01:55:00Z.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client (mobile SDK) opens many concurrent streaming upload sessions during warmup.
2) SDK bursts WINDOW_UPDATE frames aggressively (observed via tcpdump) causing apigw to schedule many half-closed streams to the runtime.
3) apigw connection coalescing holds sockets in accept queue; keepalive-reaper aggressively cleans idle keepalives.
4) runtime processes hit per-process FD limit as connections transition states -> runtime triggers watchdog restart and OOM-like tears (SIGABRT in logs).
5) apigw returns 502/503 to callers while runtime restarts loop for affected shard.

Observed logs / metrics:
- apigw metrics: accept_queue_depth spiked from 50 -> 5,200 in 3 minutes.
- api error-rate (eu-west): 0.2% -> 14% (02:10–02:30 UTC).
- runtime logs: repeated "EMFILE: too many open files" and watchdog timeout traces referencing shard-12 worker pid 14233.
- tcpdump: bursts of HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE from specific mobile SDK versions (iOS-sdk v3.6.1).
- Correlation: spike starts ~15m after keepalive-reaper v2.3.1 rollout.

Initial hypotheses considered:
- Kernel-level FD leak in runtime.
- apigw connection coalescing regression interacting poorly with aggressive client WINDOW_UPDATE bursts.
- Keepalive reaper change introduced more aggressive socket churn leaving half-closed descriptors allocated.

Investigation steps and findings:
- Rolled pprof and FD snapshots on runtime: per-process open FD counts grew linearly during the burst; many FDs in CLOSE_WAIT and half-closed states.
- Reproduced WINDOW_UPDATE burst in staging by running a mobile-sdk traffic emulator -> accept_queue grew and runtime FD counts increased.
- Reviewed keepalive-reaper v2.3.1 diff: introduced new aggressive cull path for sockets idle > 30s that interacts with apigw's socket-sliding-window -> created a race where sockets were removed from apigw tracking but not closed in runtime immediately.
- Identified a subtle bug in apigw socket handoff codepath where a reclaimed keepalive could leave the runtime with a duplicate file descriptor reference until the next GC; the fd count never decremented under heavy churn.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Immediately rolled back apigw keepalive-reaper to v2.3.0 in eu-west at 02:35 UTC (rollback PR: github.com/redwood-inference/apigw/PR#5905).
- Increased runtime worker per-process fd soft limit from 32k -> 64k for customer pool-12 as a breathing room measure.
- Coordinated with customer to throttle client warmup (suggested staggered startup window and SDK v3.6.2 beta with backoff).

Resolution and long-term fixes deployed:
- Root cause: race between keepalive-reaper aggressive cull + apigw handoff bug causing FDs to accumulate in CLOSE_WAIT and not be reclaimed promptly, leading to runtime watchdog restarts and a 5xx wave.
- Fixes committed: apigw PR#5891 (fix socket-handoff race) and reaper PR#5902 (tuned cull thresholds + added backpressure signals).
- Deploy timeline: patch rolled to eu-west (canary 03:10 UTC), monitored for 2 hours with no recurrence. Full rollout completed 2026-03-12T05:20:00Z.
- Post-fix: error-rate returned to baseline (<0.3%) and accept_queue steady-state returned to pre-incident levels.

Post-incident actions / follow-ups:
- Postmortem doc scheduled in Confluence: confluence.redwood.ai/INC/2026-03-12-acceptqueue-fd-exhaustion (owner: Marco Silva).
- Add unit/integration tests for apigw socket handoff to prevent duplicate-FD scenarios.
- Add automated staging test that simulates WINDOW_UPDATE bursts from client SDKs.
- Improve monitoring: add alert for per-process FD >= 75% of soft limit and apigw accept_queue growth > 1,000 for 2m.

Customer communication notes:
- CS notified customer at 02:42 UTC that we had applied a rollback and a breathing-room config.
- At 06:00 UTC sent a follow-up with root cause summary and timeline, included suggested client mitigations (upgrade SDK and stagger warmup).

resolution_summary: Rolled back aggressive keepalive reaper, patched apigw socket-handoff race, increased runtime FD soft limit as emergency mitigation, and fully rolled out fixes to eu-west. Customer services returned to baseline. Postmortem and tests scheduled.
root_cause: Race condition between apigw socket handoff and new keepalive reaper culling behavior caused sockets to remain referenced on runtime leading to per-process fd exhaustion and runtime watchdog restarts, which generated elevated 5xx responses.
next_steps: Implement regression tests for socket handoff and WINDOW_UPDATE burst in CI/staging
Add FD-level alerting and runbook for rapid mitigation
Coordinate SDK team to push backoff mitigation in next mobile SDK release
Close follow-up task after postmortem action items are complete
